teams.synopsis: A narrow win over Deniz, even without Mike Williams - this offense doesn't have a weak link.
teams.blurb: A dominant showing in Week 8 allowed Malich to narrowly defeat Deniz. Despite having no <mark class="hl-player">Mike Williams</mark>, this team is able to produce monster numbers, and I don't see how this team won't continue to win games.

teams.synopsis: A bye-week dip, but still the highest PF in the league and a clear playoff favorite.
teams.blurb: A down week in Week 8 for this team may have been due to byes, but this team is still very talented and has the highest PF. I do expect another fall next week, though, because of byes again - but this team is definitely a favorite to make the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: The Hockenson trade quietly helps Amon-Ra - and Brandon looks like he's turning a corner.
teams.blurb: I brought Brandon back up this week because of his production in Week 8, but also because <mark class="hl-player">Amon-Ra</mark> is now free of <mark class="hl-player">Hockenson</mark> taking targets, and I feel like Hockenson might be better off with the Vikings anyway. Might be a debatable placement, but I feel like Brandon might be turning it around and proving the doubters wrong.

teams.synopsis: A 3-5 record undersells this ceiling - the second half should look very different.
teams.blurb: Despite losing last week, this team is still very good and has shown the ability to put up absurd numbers any given week. Even though he sits at 3-5, I predict Deniz to have a solid second half of the season and make the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: A rough stretch for one of the league's steadiest teams, but the playoff lock status holds.
teams.blurb: A bit of a fall for one of the only positive teams - Andrew's team has been struggling recently, but I don't think that lasts long. This team shouldn't be forgotten about and is almost a lock for the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: Still mourning Breece - the talent's there, but the trajectory has this one worried.
teams.blurb: Still sad over the loss of Breece. Quad's team is still very talented and definitely has the opportunity to make the playoffs this year. That being said, I don't like the direction this team is moving in, and we could be seeing a downfall.

teams.synopsis: Injuries, byes, and a brutal remaining schedule - this week is close to a must-win.
teams.blurb: Carmine has been plagued with injuries and byes the past couple weeks, and with a very tough rest-of-season schedule, this team will need a win this week for the playoffs to look possible.

teams.synopsis: ETN's upside and Taylor's bust season pulling in opposite directions.
teams.blurb: Back down the list this week, Anthony's team is a weird one. On one end, he has a very promising RB for the rest of the season in <mark class="hl-player">ETN</mark>, but on the other, <mark class="hl-player">Taylor</mark> has been the biggest bust in fantasy. Will we start to see this team lose in the upcoming weeks?

teams.synopsis: Ranked 13th and took it personally - a 160-point explosion says a playoff push is brewing.
teams.blurb: After being ranked 13th last week, this team took it personally. They exploded for 160 points and dominated the week. I expect this team to come back down to earth in Week 9 with Barkley on bye, but we could be seeing a sneaky playoff push from Baylen.

teams.synopsis: Finally cracked the top 10 - the question now is whether it's sustainable.
teams.blurb: Finally in the top 10 - Geg's team deserves it after a very solid Week 8, but is it sustainable? I'm worried about <mark class="hl-player">Cooks</mark> for the rest of the season, and <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> once <mark class="hl-player">Deebo</mark> comes back, but nonetheless, this team has the ability to put up numbers that can win weeks.

teams.synopsis: Better than the record shows, but no superstar name to lean on when it matters.
teams.blurb: I think this team is very solid and has the ability to win any given week, but the lack of superstar talent scares me a bit. <mark class="hl-player">Cook</mark> is a big name, but not enough to carry a team on his own. This team has been very good all season, and the record doesn't accurately reflect the team's production, but I think the unluckiness might be too much and slowly crush Quigley's playoff aspirations.

teams.synopsis: A surprise fall - Robinson hasn't lived up to the hype, and the ceiling looks capped.
teams.blurb: Falling in the ranking was a surprise to me, but <mark class="hl-player">Robinson</mark> might not be as good as we predicted, and we don't know how injuries will affect this team. I still value Gorman as a good team and a possible playoff squad, but his ceiling is capped.

teams.synopsis: Only Josh Allen is carrying his weight - an Adams trade might be the reset button.
teams.blurb: This entire team is underperforming besides <mark class="hl-player">Josh Allen</mark>, which is why I think trades are inevitable. Ben reportedly wants an 'RB and WR' for <mark class="hl-player">Adams</mark>, so start hitting his line if you want. Keep an eye on <mark class="hl-player">Fournette</mark> - will his production be sustainable for the rest of the season? Again, a solid squad, but the former champion would need luck on his side to go back-to-back this year.

teams.synopsis: A win didn't move the needle, but Moore and Foreman show flickers of life.
teams.blurb: Still the last team despite winning in Week 8 - Cole's team has sort of come alive, with <mark class="hl-player">Moore</mark> being fantasy-relevant again and <mark class="hl-player">Foreman</mark> potentially being a solid RB2 as well. That being said, this team still has the least PF and is tied for the worst record in the league, so I have to give him this spot.
